Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today 

	really productive. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC:

Call recap (high level)
- Use case: customer support augmentation + semantic search + prioritized reranker for KB retrieval.
- Goals: improve first-response accuracy, reduce mean time to resolution, and ensure safe outputs for regulated data.
- POC scope: embed ~200k docs, serve search+reranker for a single product line, deploy in our US region.

Open items / asks for engineering follow-up (please confirm):
1) Auth & SDK: Are you planning to use API keys from Redwood Dedicated, or do you want to integrate via your OIDC provider (we support both)? Any constraints from your security team?
2) Routing & model variants: Do you want deterministic routing (pin to a single model) or policy-based routing (latency fallback/cost tiers)?
3) Structured output & tool calling: We showed the structured output example during the demo. Can you share the canonical JSON schema you want the model to return for the KB reranker + agent?
4) Embeddings + reranker: Are you planning to use dense vector search only, or a hybrid approach with lexical fallbacks? What's your expected qps for the POC?
5) Prompt governance: You asked about versioning and injection mitigations 

	would love to connect you with our solutions engineer to propose a concrete governance flow and red-team checklist.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi (cc) to send a short integration note (SDK snippets + auth + routing examples) and a sample prompt governance template by EOD tomorrow.
- You share the schema for structured output and any security/SSO constraints.
- Schedule a 60-min technical workshop next week to wire up the first embedding job.

Attachments: architecture diagram (acme-integration-arch.png) and our SOC2 summary.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ACME - Integration & Prompt Governance follow-up

Hi Sam / Priya - thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise integration plan + examples that address SDK auth, routing, structured output, embeddings/reranker, and prompt governance (versioning + injection mitigations). Attaching a sample prompt governance JSON (prompt-governance-sample.json) and the integration architecture diagram (acme-integration-arch.png).

1) SDK & Auth
- We provide first-class SDKs (Python/Node) and a simple REST API. For production we recommend OIDC token exchange to issue short-lived inference tokens. For POC: programmatic API keys are fine.
- Example (pseudo-code):
  # Python (requests)
  token = oidc_client.exchange_assertion(assertion)
  headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
  payload = {"model": "redwood-rlhf-3b", "input": prompt}
  r = requests.post("https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/generate", headers=headers, json=payload)

- Rotation: we support a key-rotation endpoint and automated rotation via our CLI.

2) Routing & model variants
- Policies available:
  a) Pin-to-model: always route to specified model/version (deterministic).
  b) Policy-based: prefer low-latency model, fallback to a higher-capacity model on overload; can include cost thresholds.
- For POC with 150 qps peak we recommend policy-based routing with a small warm pool of dedicated capacity for critical routes to reduce cold-starts.

3) Structured output & tool calling
- We enforce schema via two mechanisms: (1) model-constrained generation using system prompts + JSON schema examples, and (2) post-generation validation with deterministic parsers.
- Example system prompt snippet:
  System prompt (versioned): 
  "You are Redwood Agent v1.3. Outputs MUST be valid JSON matching the schema: {\"answer\": string, \"confidence_score\": number, \"kb_article_id\": string|null, \"actions\": [ {\"type\": string, \"payload\": object } ] }. If the model cannot answer, return \"answer\": \"I don't know\" and actions: []"

- SDK snippet (NodeJS) showing tool call with structured output enforcement:
  const response = await redwood.generate({
    model: 'redwood-agent-1.3',
    input: userQuestion,
    enforceSchema: true, // SDK flag that runs parse + validation
    tools: [{ name: 'kb_lookup', schema: {...} }]
  })

4) Embeddings + reranker strategy
- Indexing: embed docs using our embeddings service. We support batching and async bulk upload.
- Retrieval: recommend hybrid: dense ANN retrieval using our vector index + lexical BM25 fallback for short queries.
- Reranker: two options
  a) Cross-encoder reranker (higher quality, higher latency) - good for top-10 candidate re-ranking.
  b) Lightweight on-the-fly reranker (distilled model) for low-latency recency-sensitive re-rank.
- For 150 qps, suggested approach: ANN retrieval to get top-100, lightweight reranker to top-10, cross-encoder for final top-3 if latency SLAs allow.

5) Prompt templates & governance (versioning + injection mitigations + red teaming)
- Versioning: maintain prompts as first-class artifacts in a Git-backed prompt registry. Naming convention: <component>-<purpose>-v{major}.{minor} e.g., agent-system-v1.3. Metadata tracked: author, commit hash, changelog, test prompts, evaluation metrics, approved-by.
- Deployment: prompts are packaged with rollout metadata; we support canary prompt rollouts (percent traffic) and automatic rollback on QA regressions.
- Injection mitigations:
  a) System prompts separate from user content and marked immutable for a given rollout.
  b) Input sanitation: escape or canonicalize user-provided delimiters and remove suspicious instruction-like patterns when incorporating external content.
  c) Output validation: enforce schema and run policy checks post-generation (block/flag outputs containing disallowed instructions).
  d) Context windows: limit the portion of external content included; use chunking + citation metadata rather than raw concatenation.
  e) Use of model-level instruction tuning: prefer models with instruction-reliability profiles for untrusted contexts.
- Red teaming: recommended red-team process:
  1) Threat modeling for each prompt (what the model can be asked to do).
  2) Generate malicious prompt candidates (automated + human) and run against the prompt set in staging.
  3) Log and classify failures (severity, exploitability).
  4) Apply mitigations (prompt rewrite, sanitizer, stricter schema, model change).
  5) Re-test and approve.
- Example prompt governance entry (high level):
  name: agent-system-v1.3
  author: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
  approved_by: sec_team_lead
  tests: [sanity_qa_harness.json, injection_redteam_suite.json]

6) Observability & auditing
- We retain prompt change history and execution traces for audit (configurable retention; default 90 days, can extend).
- For compliance: provide exports of prompt artifact histories and per-request metadata (model, prompt_version, routing_policy).

7) POC checklist (actionable)
- Acme provides: structured output schema + Auth0 test tenant credentials + representative doc set (sample 10k docs).
- Redwood provides: sample code (SDK) for OIDC exchange, integration diagram, prompt governance template, embedding job config, and a reranker config.
- Schedule: 60-min workshop to run first embed job, target Wed next week.

Attachments included: prompt-governance-sample.json (contains sample registry entry + tests), acme-integration-arch.png. Also attaching our SOC2 summary for your security review (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).

If helpful, I can also include a copy of a canary rollout plan and a short red-team checklist. Happy to discuss in the workshop.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
